nar.text: Arcangeli's right rear tyre is cut by an official's car before the start; he changes it at the Cremona pits and returns to the grid.
Roberto Farinacci and Count Romeo Gallenga (Note 1) finally gave the start at 15:28 for the cars over 1500 cc.
Ten minutes after the large cars had started, the 1500 cc cars were sent away.
At the front was the red Alfa of Campari, 50 meters ahead of Varzi, Nuvolari and Bona, after another 100 meters there followed a close group of Arcangeli, Saccomanni and Alverà.
Materassi leads the 1500 cc cars past the Cremona grandstands.
Serboli in the Delage was already missing.
Materassi covers the flying 10 km in 2m53.6s, the first to beat Ascari's record.
At the end of the first lap, Campari passed the finish after 21m35s at 175.079 km/h average speed
Campari pits to change both front tyres, losing 3m30s.
Arcangeli passed in 22m46.2s, passing Campari in the pits and taking the lead, followed by Nuvolari and Materassi.
After his first lap Nuvolari followed Campari into the pits for tires.
Arcangeli was leading the second lap, one minute ahead of Materassi, more than two minutes ahead of Nuvolari and over three minutes to Saccomani in fourth place.
Campari sets a new flying 10 km record of 2m45.4s.
Campari changes tyres again at the end of the lap and falls over 15 minutes behind.
Varzi and Bona had retired at the beginning of the second lap, while Rosti, Platè and Ghersi did not return to the pits, the latter when stranded with a puncture.
Alverà, Tonini and Faccetti also retired.
Materassi followed one minute behind and Nuvolari attempted to catch up with the drivers ahead.
Fagioli and Fisauli retired their Maseratis
Nuvolari, 2m33.2s behind Arcangeli, has passed Materassi, who lost time in the pits.
Campari also ended his race at his pit after completing the fourth lap when he was over half an hour behind.
Giovanardi stops for good at the end of lap four.
Nenzioni retired on the fifth lap.
Arcangeli wins ahead of Nuvolari; Materassi third and 1500 class winner, Saccomani fourth.
Materassi had to change tires twice while Arcangeli arrived victorious with four tires in good condition
